successCriteria.description: A token-verification utility resolves with an object carrying userId and role (both strings) when given a JWT signed with the process.env JWT_SECRET; it rejects (does not resolve) for invalid, tampered, or expired tokens.
A header-parsing utility returns the raw token string when given a well-formed "Bearer <token>" Authorization header value, and returns null when the header is absent, empty, or not in Bearer scheme.
An authentication preHandler, on a request with a valid Bearer token, attaches the verified user identity (userId + role) to the request so downstream handlers can read it type-safely.

The authentication preHandler, on a missing, malformed, or invalid/expired token, sends a 401 response directly via the reply object and does not proceed to the route handler (no unhandled rejection reaches the runtime).

A role-gating preHandler factory, given one or more allowed role strings, returns a preHandler that permits the request when the authenticated user's role is among the allowed set and sends a 403 response directly when the role does not match.
The role-gating preHandler sends a 401 response (not 403) when no authenticated user is present on the request, so "not authenticated" is distinguishable from "authenticated but insufficient role".

Fastify's request type is augmented so that an optional user identity (userId + role) is visible to TypeScript under strict mode, allowing downstream code to read request.user.userId without type errors.
A barrel entry point re-exports the JWT utilities, the preHandler middleware, and the type augmentation so that consumers import only through that single module surface.

Unit tests cover the token-verification utility (valid token, invalid token, expired token) and the header-parsing utility (valid Bearer, missing header, non-Bearer scheme) using plain Jest with relative imports and no setup files.

Unit tests cover the authentication preHandler (attaches user on success, sends 401 on missing/invalid token) and the role-gating preHandler (permits matching role, sends 403 on mismatch, sends 401 when unauthenticated), with the JWT verification mocked.

constraints: No hardcoded secrets — JWT_SECRET must be read from process.env at runtime, never embedded as a literal in source (HARNESS.json no-hardcoded-secrets, critical).
No use of `any` — use `unknown` with type guards instead (HARNESS.json no-any, high severity); the JwtPayload index signature must not leak `any` into the public return type.
RBAC is enforced at middleware (preHandler), never inline in route handlers or business logic (GP-005, AGENTS.md architecture rule 4).
No sensitive data in logs — tokens must never be logged (GP-004); error responses must not echo the raw token value.

No unhandled promise rejections — the synchronous jsonwebtoken verify that throws must be wrapped so failures are caught and surfaced as controlled error replies, never as unhandled rejections (GP-006).

Modules import only through their declared public entry point (index.ts barrel); the auth module's internals (jwt.ts, middleware.ts, types.ts) are consumed via the barrel, not via deep imports (AGENTS.md architecture rule 1).
Error replies are sent directly via the reply object (reply.code/status + send), not by throwing, because no global Fastify error handler is registered in src/app.ts.
Shared utilities live under src/shared/; the auth module resides at src/shared/auth/ consistent with the existing src/shared/db and src/shared/errorTypes layout.
TypeScript strict mode applies — no implicit any, strict null checks; the augmented request.user must be optional to reflect that unauthenticated requests have no user.

Tests use plain Jest (describe/it/expect) with relative imports from the tests directory and no extra setup files, matching the established test style in tests/unit/shared/errorTypes.test.ts and jest.config.js testMatch.
outOfScope: Registering the authenticate/requireRole preHandlers on any route or in src/app.ts — that is Phase 8 (leave routes and app registration).
Implementing the /auth login or token-issuance endpoints (jwt.sign for production token creation) — this phase only verifies tokens; issuing tokens is out of scope.
Leave controller, leave service, leave routes, and any leave-domain business logic — those are Phases 6–8.
OIDC / corporate identity provider integration — production identity comes from corporate OIDC per ARCHITECTURE.md; this phase handles local JWT verification only.
A global Fastify error handler or setErrorHandler — the settled decision is direct reply-based error responses; no global handler is added this phase.
Refresh-token logic, token blacklisting/revocation, or session management — only stateless JWT verification is in scope.

entityInvariants.invariant: A successfully verified identity always carries a non-empty userId and a role string; it can only be produced by verifying a token signed with the process.env JWT_SECRET, and it is immutable once attached to a request.

After the authentication preHandler runs successfully, the request carries exactly one verified user identity; before it runs (or after it fails with a 401), the request has no user identity. The presence of request.user is the sole signal that authentication succeeded.

A role gate is a preHandler factory parameterized by an allowed-roles set; it admits a request only when an authenticated user's role is a member of that set, and it never mutates the user identity — it only permits or denies.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Verify a JWT and return the embedded user identity
interfaceConstraints.authRule: Uses process.env JWT_SECRET as the verification key; no caller-supplied secret.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Rejects the returned Promise (does not resolve) for any jsonwebtoken failure (JsonWebTokenError, TokenExpiredError, NotBeforeError) or when required claims are absent; never throws synchronously to the caller.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Extract a bearer token from an Authorization header value
interfaceConstraints.authRule: Pure function with no side effects; does not verify the token, only parses the Bearer scheme.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns null (never throws) when the header is undefined, empty, or not in "Bearer <token>" form.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Reads the Authorization header from the request, extracts and verifies the bearer token, and attaches the verified identity to the request on success.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: On missing/malformed/invalid/expired token, sends a 401 response directly via the reply object and short-circuits (does not call the route handler); no exception escapes the hook.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Gate a request by allowed roles (preHandler factory)
interfaceConstraints.authRule: Checks the authenticated user's role against the supplied allowed-roles set; requires that authentication has already run (user identity present on the request).
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Sends 401 directly when no authenticated user is present; sends 403 directly when the user's role is not in the allowed set; permits the request otherwise. No exception escapes the hook.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Auth-failure semantics must align with the existing UnauthorizedError (401) and ForbiddenError (403) classes: 401 for missing/invalid/expired tokens (unauthenticated) and 403 for insufficient role (authenticated but forbidden), matching the HTTP-mapping table already documented for these error types.

Environment-variable loading must follow the established precedent: read JWT_SECRET from process.env at runtime (dotenv.config() is already invoked at import time in connection.ts, establishing the env-loading pattern for src/shared/).

The auth module's barrel export must follow the same re-export pattern used by existing module barrels (src/modules/leave/index.ts, src/modules/uptime/index.ts): a single index.ts re-exporting all public symbols so consumers import only through the barrel.

Error responses must be sent directly via reply.status(n).send(...) / reply.code(n).send(...), matching the existing route-handler pattern in uptime.routes.ts where replies are sent directly and no global error handler is relied upon.

Unit tests must follow the established test style: plain describe/it/expect with relative imports from the tests directory and no setup files, matching tests/unit/shared/errorTypes.test.ts and the jest.config.js testMatch glob.

The verified identity shape (userId + role) and the role-gating contract (requireRole accepting 'manager' and 'admin') must match what downstream Phase 7–8 consumers expect: controllers read request.user.userId and routes apply requireRole('manager','admin') for approve/reject/pending endpoints.

integrationPoints.why: The verification utility wraps the synchronous, throwing jwt.verify in a Promise to present an async interface; jwt.sign is available for test helpers to mint tokens.

authenticate and requireRole are Fastify preHandler hooks that read request.headers.authorization, attach request.user, and send error replies via the reply object; they integrate with the route lifecycle so downstream handlers only run on success.
Controllers will read the authenticated user's userId from the augmented request to attribute submit/approve/reject/cancel actions; the type augmentation must make this type-safe.

Route registration will apply the authenticate preHandler and the role-gating preHandler to protected endpoints; the role-gating contract must accept the 'manager' and 'admin' role strings used downstream.
The verification key is read from the environment at runtime, consistent with the dotenv precedent; tests must set/restore this variable rather than hardcoding a secret.
